guarantees.claim: digest_size equals digest_size_supplied when it is SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512; otherwise digest_size is SHA2_None.

assumptions.claim: digest_size_supplied must be a valid 2‑state value (no X or Z) for the case mapping to be deterministic.
assumptions.risk: X/Z on digest_size_supplied may cause digest_size to become unknown, risking security‑critical state machine misbehaviour or error masking.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment states that an unsupported digest size blocks HMAC/SHA‑2 start and signals an error to software. This logic is not present in this chunk; a different module must detect digest_size == SHA2_None and enforce the error/block behaviour.
uncertain_points.cond: when digest_size_supplied is an unsupported value
uncertain_points.risk: If downstream logic does not detect SHA2_None and block the engine, an attacker could force the HMAC to operate with an unsupported digest size, potentially causing incorrect digest computation or bypassing security checks.
